_comment: Backdated finds and verdicts for the demo tenant.
Why this file exists: verify windows are ~14 days. Seeding only 'today'
would leave the ledger with nothing but pending predictions — no verified
wins, no misses, no hit rate — and the ledger is the most important screen
in the product. This gives it a real track record on first run.
Every find cites observations from observations.json by id, so the evidence
trail is genuine: each recommendation is traceable to the retrieved rows
The espresso find is deliberately a MISS built on thin evidence. That is the
honest shape of the product — the agent reasoned from a weak signal, was
wrong, and the ledger says so permanently.
created_days_ago is relative to the seed run; verify_window_days is added to
the creation date. A find whose window has not elapsed stays unjudged and

finds.title: Tiramisu → $9
finds.rationale: Fourteen separate reviews single out the tiramisu as the best in the city, several explicitly calling it underpriced. The eleven-restaurant survey puts the local average at $10.60 with the nearest rival at $11; Rosa's sits at $7.00 against a $2.10 food cost. Raising to $9 stays below every comparable and leaves the value perception intact.
finds.move: Reprice tiramisu from $7.00 to $9.00 and reprint the dessert card.

ledger.method: item-level dessert sales from the payment terminal, 14 days before vs after
ledger.note: 233 tiramisu sold in the period at the new price with no measurable drop in dessert attach rate.

finds.title: Text-ahead waitlist for Saturdays
finds.rationale: Twelve reviews describe abandoning or nearly abandoning a Saturday visit, and several name the absence of a waitlist specifically. Two of the three nearest rivals now advertise text-ahead or reservations. At 110 Saturday covers and a $38 average check, recovering even a handful of walkaways per night pays for itself immediately.
finds.move: Stand up a text-when-ready waitlist for Saturday service and put a sign on the door.

ledger.method: counted seated parties originating from the waitlist, valued at average check
ledger.note: 41 parties seated from the waitlist over two weeks that would previously have been standing at the door.

finds.title: Espresso upsell after dessert
finds.rationale: Dessert-only and late-evening visits are a growing share of local independent traffic, and the wine list already reads well. Prompting an espresso alongside dessert is a zero-cost add with a high margin.
finds.move: Have servers offer espresso with every dessert order.

ledger.method: item-level espresso sales from the payment terminal, 14 days before vs after
ledger.note: No measurable lift. Espresso interest locally is flat and the evidence for this was thin — two weakly related observations. Pulled after four days.

finds.title: Voicemail with text callback
finds.rationale: Six reviews describe being unable to reach anyone by phone, including one lost large-party booking and one lost whole-cake order. The owner has said they cannot answer during service. A voicemail greeting that invites a text, answered between seatings, converts those calls instead of losing them.
finds.move: Record a voicemail greeting directing callers to text, and check it twice per service.

ledger.method: bookings and large orders attributed to returned calls, valued at recorded ticket totals
ledger.note: Recovered two large-party bookings and four cake orders in the period.

finds.title: Open the patio every warm night
finds.rationale: Six reviews mention the patio, three of them describing it closed on a night that would have suited it. Local search interest in patio dining is up thirty four percent and the forecast holds twenty two consecutive evenings above sixty five degrees. Twenty additional seats at 54 percent food margin, with no new labour if set up before service.
finds.move: Set the patio before service on any evening forecast above sixty five degrees.

ledger.method: covers seated on the patio, valued at average check less food cost
ledger.note: Patio ran eleven of fourteen nights and averaged fourteen extra covers on those nights.

finds.title: Reply to every recent low review
finds.rationale: The one and two star reviews cluster almost entirely on Saturday waits and unanswered phone calls — both now addressed. Replying to each one publicly, naming the fix, converts the strongest objection a prospective diner will read into evidence that the place listens.
finds.move: Draft a reply to each one and two star review from the last ninety days for the owner to approve.

ledger.method: new-diner covers modelled against the rating change over the period
ledger.note: Rating moved from 4.2 to 4.3 over two weeks with nineteen replies posted.

finds.title: Tuesday–Thursday three-course set menu
finds.rationale: The owner reports Tuesday through Thursday as consistently weakest, with four of eleven nearby restaurants now running midweek promotions and one direct rival at a $45 prix fixe. A set menu at a lower price point fills seats that are otherwise empty, at controlled food cost.
finds.move: Design a three-course midweek set menu and price it against the rival's $45.

ledger.method: midweek covers and set-menu attach rate from the payment terminal
ledger.note: Midweek covers up nine per night on average across the period.

finds.title: Late dessert window, 9pm to 10pm
finds.rationale: Dessert and late-evening visits are a growing share of local traffic, and weekend demand peaks sharply at 7pm to 8:30pm — leaving the last hour underused with the kitchen already staffed. A dessert-and-drink-only window monetises seats that would otherwise turn over empty.
finds.move: Advertise a dessert-and-drinks-only window for the last hour of service.

ledger.method: modelled from dessert attach rate; item-level verification pending at month end
ledger.note: Not yet verifiable — the measurement window closes at month end. Shown as an estimate rather than counted as a win.

finds.title: Lunch service, Tuesday to Thursday
finds.rationale: Ten separate observations show unmet midday demand around the courthouse, including a forum thread where nine people gave up and ate at their desks. Nine of eleven nearby Italian restaurants already serve lunch; Rosa's is one of the two that do not. A nine-storey office confirmed for September occupancy adds roughly four hundred daytime workers within two blocks. This is the largest single opportunity in the corpus.
finds.move: Build a limited lunch menu from existing prep and open Tuesday to Thursday, 11am to 2pm, before the office opens in September.

finds.title: Validated parking at the nearby garage
finds.rationale: Eight reviews mention parking difficulty, consistently paired with praise for the food — diners are arriving despite it rather than being turned away by it. No new public capacity is planned. A validation deal would improve the experience but the evidence does not support a large revenue effect, and the cost sits against the owner's monthly cap.
finds.move: Approach the garage two doors down about a validation rate for diners.

finds.title: Raise pasta mains by $2
finds.rationale: Seven separate reviews describe the prices as low — two of them unprompted, one saying outright that the bill comes in lower than expected. Osteria Bianca runs $24 to $32 against Rosa's $18 to $24, and Trattoria Nona raised its mains two dollars across the board this month with no visible complaint. Average dessert prices in the area are already up eight percent since spring. At roughly 38 pasta covers a night a two dollar rise carries almost entirely to margin. Owner rule requires approval before any price change, so this stays a proposal.
finds.move: Raise pasta mains by $2.00 across the board and reprint the dinner menu.

finds.title: Second server on Friday and Saturday peak
finds.rationale: Six reviews describe one server covering the entire floor, and the complaints are about pace rather than warmth — the same reviews praise the staff. Local diners increasingly abandon a restaurant over wait time. Saturday runs 110 covers against a kitchen that pushes fifteen per fifteen minutes, so the constraint is front of house, not the line. A second server for the 6pm to 9pm block costs roughly $51 a day averaged across the week; the prediction is net of that.
finds.move: Add a second floor server for the 6pm to 9pm block on Friday and Saturday.

finds.title: Take reservations Thursday to Saturday
finds.rationale: Seven of eleven comparable restaurants nearby advertise either reservations or a text waitlist, and Osteria Bianca posts a two week booking window. This is distinct from the waitlist already running: the waitlist manages people who have already arrived, while reservations capture the diner who will not risk the trip. One reviewer drove over to check whether the patio was open, found it closed, and left. Limiting it to the three busiest nights keeps the floor flexible on the weak midweek nights.
finds.move: Open a reservation book for Thursday, Friday and Saturday, holding four tables back for walk-ins.

finds.title: Whole tiramisu to order, 48 hours ahead
finds.rationale: A customer tried to order a whole tiramisu for a birthday, could not reach anyone, and gave up — that is a named lost sale, not an inference. Fourteen reviews single the dessert out as the best in the city, and local search for tiramisu peaks in the evening. Food cost is $2.10 a portion, so a whole cake sold at $48 carries an unusually high margin and uses prep and skill that already exist. Small, but it costs nothing to try.
finds.move: Offer whole tiramisu at $48 with 48 hours notice, taken by text, and add a line to the dessert card.

finds.title: Ask regulars for reviews at the check
finds.rationale: Osteria Bianca sits at 4.1 stars against Rosa's 4.2 but on roughly triple the review count, which means it outranks Rosa's in local results despite being rated lower. Fifteen reviews describe an unusually warm room and staff who remember people, so the goodwill exists and is simply not being converted into review volume. This is the cheapest find on the board: a printed card at the check and nothing else.
finds.move: Print a card for the check asking happy regulars to leave a review, and hand it out Thursday through Sunday.
